back: Resistances in series across a supply, sharing the p.d. in proportion to resistance; the output is taken across one of them.
$V_{\text{out}} = V_{\text{in}} \dfrac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}$ (output across $R_2$, no current drawn)
A potentiometer across the supply gives 0 V to the full supply p.d.; a series rheostat cannot reach 0 V.
NTC thermistor + fixed resistor; output across the fixed resistor rises as temperature rises.
LDR + fixed resistor; output across the LDR rises as it gets darker.
A load across the output is in parallel with R₂, lowering the output; use a load resistance ≫ R₂.
Similar to the sensor's resistance at the point of interest gives maximum sensitivity; make it variable to set the threshold.
Only the ratio of the resistances (and V_in); scaling both resistors changes the current, not the output.
